newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - Feb 25.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Today in an unprecedented alert Chief Medical Officer Sir Kenneth Calman has warned that under the auspices of bogus doctor Godwin Onubogu and the Iketam Clinical Laboratories in Balham High Road, countless cancer and HIV tests are worthless and must be retaken urgently.
LABOUR MAY FORCE US POWER BUY LISTINGS

U.S. power groups may be required to list their British subsidiaries on the London Stock Exchange by a future Labour government. The move is seen by Labour as a way of ensuring that the regional companies can be brought under regulatory control by electricity watchdog Offer.
SALVESEN REBELS SET OUT PLAN FOR GROWTH

The planned break-up of the haulage group Christian Salvesen by rebel shareholders would leave a 'dog' company too weak to survive on its own, it was warned today. The rebels today outlined a growth plan for the company, including buying up small hauliers, reviewing the senior management team and expanding the product range of Aggreko generator hire business.
BT was said to be near to closing a deal with Telstra, the Australian Telecoms carrier. The deal would help BT deliver an Asia-Pacific branch in its international strategy.
STRONG POUND SLOWS THE HOTELS CHECK-IN
Britain's hoteliers have been hit by the strong pound this year, with a number of hotel groups noticing that London business in particular was quieter in the first few weeks of January.
